lighting.colour_management: Cycles CPU seed 0, Standard view transform, exposure 0, gamma 1

v4_recalibration.reason: V3 read as dark brown opaque smoked glass. Root cause found in V4: the bottle was modelled EMPTY, so all colour had to come from the glass itself — which physically saturates to brown/red over the long base path. V4 keeps the glass only lightly tinted + frosted and adds the serum fill, giving an even warm-orange body, a lighter empty neck and NO dark-red base band
v4_recalibration.backdrop: grey 0.60 + dedicated backdrop wash light (9.0e5 W) so transmitted background is luminous

serum_fill.why: the real bottle is FILLED (IMG_3120) — the even warm body colour and the lighter empty neck come from the contents; an empty amber shell can only saturate to the rejected red base band
serum_fill.shader: Principled transmission 1.0, IOR 1.36, roughness 0.03 + Volume Absorption [1.0,0.66,0.02] @ 0.11/mm (solved from Beer-Lambert: transmitted = exp(-d*(1-colour)*path) targeted at R~1.0 G~0.5 B~0.1 over the ~30 mm body path)

glass_construction.strategy: single revolved closed manifold: outer surface + mouth rim + inner cavity surface + inner floor
